name: TKO Group
description: TKO owns and runs the UFC (mixed martial arts), WWE (scripted 'sports entertainment' shows such as Raw, SmackDown and WrestleMania), Professional Bull Riders, a boxing joint venture (Zuffa Boxing), and since February 28, 2025 the IMG and On Location businesses bought from Endeavor (media rights sales for other sports, studios, event management, sports and hospitality packages). The value is in owned content that media companies pay to distribute: UFC and WWE together earned about $1.9B in media rights, production and content fees in 2025, from partners including Paramount, ESPN, Netflix (exclusive global home of Raw since January 2025), Versant and the CW. Fights and shows cost little relative to those fees, so UFC (about 57 percent adjusted EBITDA margin) and WWE (about 52 percent) are highly profitable; IMG is a much lower-margin agency and hospitality business (about 12 percent). Endeavor and affiliates hold about 63 percent of the votes; the company also pays a large dividend and has a buyback.

businessLines.name: UFC
businessLines.how: Broadcasters and streamers (e.g. Paramount, ESPN, others) pay multi-year media rights fees to show UFC events; fans and sponsors pay for tickets, hospitality and partnerships; consumer products licensing adds a little. Costs are fighter pay and production, so most media fees drop to profit.
businessLines.description: Mixed martial arts promotion: more than 40 live events a year broadcast in over 170 countries and territories; about 650 athletes who are independent contractors.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $801.0M. Adjusted EBITDA, not operating income (TKO reports segment Adjusted EBITDA). Share is of segments' sum $1,907.5M.

businessLines.name: WWE
businessLines.how: Netflix, ESPN, Versant/USA Network and the CW pay rights fees for weekly shows and premium live events; fans pay for live event tickets and hospitality; sponsors pay for partnerships; licensing and merchandise add revenue. The rights fees are contracted over multiple years and are the main profit driver.
businessLines.description: Weekly programs Raw, SmackDown and NXT, premium live events such as WrestleMania, live event tours, WWE Network content, consumer products.

businessLines.name: IMG (with On Location and PBR)
businessLines.how: Sports leagues and event owners pay IMG commissions and fees to sell their media rights, produce content and manage events (320 clients with events in 2025); corporate and consumer buyers pay On Location for hospitality packages at major events; PBR earns media, ticket and sponsorship revenue. Much lower margin than UFC and WWE because costs (hospitality, production, client payouts) are large.
businessLines.description: Acquired from Endeavor on February 28, 2025: IMG (sports media rights sales, studios and production, event management, licensing and representation), On Location (premium hospitality for events) and Professional Bull Riders.
